ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a broken line of the open-loop logarithmic amplitude-frequency characteristic of a minimum-phase system, the vertical axis is labeled L0(ω), the horizontal line is 0 dB, and the intersection point of the broken line at 0 dB is marked as ω=2; there is a break at ω=10, the slope before the break is marked as -2, and the slope after the break is marked as -3. Reasoning: From the 0 dB crossing point, the cutoff frequency is obtained as ωc=2. The slope changes from -2 to -3, and the system is minimum phase, so it can be written as G(s)=K/[s^2(1+s/10)], where the positive real constant K only affects the magnitude and does not affect the phase. At ωc=2, the phase is ∠G(j2)=-2×90°-atan(2/10)≈-180°-11°=-191°. Therefore the phase margin γc=180°+∠G(j2)≈180°-191°=-11°.

raw_record.question_text: Given the open-loop logarithmic magnitude-frequency characteristic (broken line) of a minimum-phase system as shown in the image, calculate the phase margin \(\gamma_c\) of the system (°). Answer with a floating-point number to one decimal place.

method.method_draft: Use the image to get omega_c = 2 from the 0 dB crossing. Model the minimum-phase open-loop transfer function as G(s)=K/[s^2(1+s/10)]. Use the 0 dB condition at omega=2 only to fix K if desired; K is positive and contributes no phase. Compute the phase at omega_c: angle G(j2) = -2*90° - atan(2/10). Then gamma_c = 180° + angle G(j2), and round to one decimal place.

method.method_draft: Start from the gain crossover read visually as omega_c=2. The slope -2 at crossover indicates two pole-at-origin contributions, giving -180°. The later change from -2 to -3 at omega=10 indicates one extra first-order pole, whose exact phase contribution at omega_c is -atan(omega_c/10). Sum the phase as -180° - atan(0.2), then add 180° to obtain the phase margin and round to one decimal place.
